titleEn: One Water Jug, One Leaf-Wrapped Meal—Let's Go!

pages.text: "Taro, let's go to the shore!" Mumu bounced on the porch, both hands empty, about to step into the yard.
"I'll collect lots of shells today!" Mumu looked toward the road. Quick-handed monkey Taro swung his jug, water sloshing. Mumu turned their ears to it. "Why are your hands empty?" Taro asked.
"The shore is only a short trip." Mumu pouted. Grandma, preparing food, set two things on the porch: a bamboo water jug and a meal wrapped in a leaf.
"The shore is sunny. What if you're thirsty?" Taro asked. Mumu's throat already seemed dry. Gulp. "Oh... that wouldn't be good."
Taro opened Mumu's two hands. "Two hands, right? One thing in each." Mumu looked at their palms.
Mumu picked up the jug in one hand. Slosh, slosh. "One hand left!" Taro slid the leaf-wrapped meal toward Mumu.
Mumu took it in the other hand. Both were full. "One Water Jug, One Leaf-Wrapped Meal—Let's Go!" Taro tapped the starting signal with his branch: tok-tok, tok-tok.
They collected lots of shells on the shore. The sun was hot, and Mumu grew thirsty. Mumu tipped the jug and drank. "I'm glad I brought it!"
Mumu held up both hands for Grandma. "One, water jug! Two, leaf-wrapped meal! When both hands are full, let's go!" Next time, Mumu filled both hands first.

They sat shoulder to shoulder, sharing the meal. Mumu folded one ear gently over Taro's shoulder. Being prepared meant none of their playtime was wasted. Mumu smiled and shook a shell. "One Water Jug, One Leaf-Wrapped Meal—Let's Go!"
